summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for intractable vomiting and found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with urosepsis. She was treated with an insulin drip, later transitioned to subcutaneous insulin, and received IV meropenem for sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was confirmed in both urine and blood cultures. A central line was placed for access and later replaced with a PICC line for outpatient antibiotic therapy with ertapenem. She developed acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 2.2, which improved to 1.1 with IV fluids. A troponin elevation to 0.2 was attributed to demand ischemia. She remained stable, did not require pressors or intubation, and was discharged home with nursing services for PICC line management after completing initial stabilization.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
